title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 126 (Right to dividend, rights shares and bonus shares to be held in abeyance pending registration of transfer of shares)

content.overview: Where any instrument of transfer of shares has been delivered to a company for registration and the transfer of such shares has not been registered by the company, it shall, notwithstanding anything contained in any other provision of this Act,— (a) transfer the dividend in relation to such shares to the Unpaid Dividend Account referred to in section 124 unless the company is authorised by the registered holder of such shares in writing to pay such dividend to the transferee specified in such instrument of transfer; and (b) keep in abeyance in relation to such shares any offer of rights shares under section 62(1)(a) and any issue of fully paid-up bonus shares in pursuance of the first proviso to section 123(5).
content.glance: Where a transfer is lodged but not registered, dividend goes to the Unpaid Dividend Account unless the registered holder authorises payment to the transferee; rights and bonus issues are kept in abeyance.
content.study:
## Section 126 — Dividend and rights/bonus pending registration of transfer

Where an instrument of transfer has been delivered for registration and the transfer has not been registered:
- **Dividend:** transfer to the Unpaid Dividend Account under section 124, unless the registered holder authorises in writing payment to the transferee.
- **Rights and bonus:** keep in abeyance any offer of rights shares under section 62(1)(a) and any fully paid-up bonus issue under the first proviso to section 123(5).

Section 126 protects the position during the registration gap. It does not decide title (see sections 56, 58 and 59).

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

sections.heading: Dividend
sections.body: Default is transfer to Unpaid Dividend Account; payment to transferee needs written authority of the registered holder.

sections.heading: Rights and bonus
sections.body: Rights offers and fully paid-up bonus issues relating to those shares are kept in abeyance pending registration.

examples.title: Lodged but unregistered transfer
examples.body: Transfer instrument delivered; not yet registered; dividend goes to Unpaid Dividend Account unless registered holder authorises payment to transferee. Educational illustration.

hypotheticals.question: Can the company pay dividend to the transferee named in a lodged but unregistered transfer?
hypotheticals.analysis: Only if the registered holder authorises payment to that transferee in writing. Otherwise the dividend is transferred to the Unpaid Dividend Account.

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 126 as deciding title to the shares.
misconceptions.correction: Section 126 deals with dividend and rights/bonus during the registration gap; title is governed by sections 56, 58 and 59.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 126 require when a transfer is lodged but not registered?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Transfer the dividend to the Unpaid Dividend Account unless the registered holder authorises payment to the transferee, and keep rights and bonus issues in abeyance for those shares.
